request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This window finishes the AL and tools session with two topics. First, a static call graph analysis in the AL tool, shown by tracing who can reach a fee calculation method through a public code unit and a page action. Second, support in production: coding agents can now start performance profiles and snapshot recordings themselves through two new MCP proxy commands. The speakers stress that the human still has to judge what the captured evidence means. The window ends with a recap of the development cycle and advice to adopt one step at a time.

chapters.title: Static call graph analysis for review
Support lifecycle step: profiles and snapshots by agents
Profiling and snapshot MCP proxies in the AL tool

features.name: Static call graph analysis (graph command in the AL tool)
features.description: The AL tool builds a graph of callers across an extension and its dependencies. You or your coding agent can query it, for example to find who calls a method, where the public boundary is, and the path from a page action to the method. The extracted output can be compared between versions and queried offline.
caveats: The extraction takes time and was done in advance for the demo
Static analysis works on the extracted data, not on the project as it is now like the LSP
A separate full session on the graph tool will cover querying and visualizing the graph in more detail
prerequisites: Run the extraction first over the apps you specify (compiles them)
The al.net tool, where the agentic tools live

features.name: Launch profiling MCP proxy
features.description: A new AL tool command that lets a coding agent start, monitor and stop a performance profile and look at the results, using the same kind of tooling and parameters as in Visual Studio Code. The agent needs to know the environment and the profile speed settings.
caveats: No actual profiling was run in the demo, only the command and its parameters were shown
The developer still has to judge what the captured evidence means
Work happens on the server, the proxy is only an interface for the client
prerequisites: An agentic framework that can use the MCP proxy

features.name: Launch snapshot MCP proxy
features.description: A new AL tool command that lets agents target a specific environment and tenant and start a snapshot recording while a user is working. This captures values and the call stack to find a bottleneck, an error or another issue. It has fewer parameters than the profiling proxy.
caveats: No snapshot is run on the client, all work happens on the server
The developer still has to judge what the evidence means
